# Pairs for pow (a function of two arguments) from CORE-MATH's published list of its hard cases: one
# pair a line, `x y`, each as its raw bits in hex (Double.doubleToRawLongBits), x first. Read by
# Inputs.hardCasePairs("pow-coremath"). Lines starting with # are comments. hard-cases/pow.txt is
# the self-computed file beside it.
#
# Source: the CORE-MATH project, https://gitlab.inria.fr/core-math/core-math, commit
# 185b7dec645407a4ded6ee01d6af14a784a17514, file src/binary64/pow/pow.wc (1003380 lines, sha256
# e3b6d6af7d5855b1196c6cf4238b3f99dc159f07be6de46a2d687514dffd8253), fetched from the URL below.
# Only input pairs are taken from it, as numeric facts. The file's notice, its lines 1-20, verbatim,
# follows the URL.
#

# Written by dev/coremath-hard-cases.py (its docstring says how to fetch the list), which checks the
# file's sha256, takes these of its lines, by the source's line numbers, in this order, and refuses
# any line that does not spell exactly one double per argument:
#   25-104: the source's first section, "worst cases" for pow: all 80 lines, 79 of them annotated
#     `# N` or `# -m N`, N the identical bits after the round bit (from 44 to 153); 52 pairs
#     written.
#   977527-990843 (N >= 110): Bernt Gombala's targeted search (wc_targeted_search_result_cases.txt):
#     13317 near-midpoint cases of 100 to 117 identical bits; those of N >= 110; 289 pairs written.
#   990862-992304 (N >= 100): Bernt Gombala's near-rational cases (wc_near_rational_cases.txt): 1443
#     cases of 90 to 153 identical bits, near a midpoint or a double; those of N >= 100; 106 pairs
#     written.
#   31265-31542: the source's "exact/midpoint cases from core-math-power/bacsel-results", y = 3/2:
#     all 278 lines, 139 exact results and 139 ties; 278 pairs written.
#   992315-999710 (the first 3 per y): Bernt Gombala's normal midpoint cases
#     (wc_norm_midpoint_cases.txt): 7396 exact ties over 41 values of y; the first 3 lines of each
#     y; 123 pairs written.
#
# A line whose pair an earlier line here already gave is not written again: 32 lines, each with the
# line it repeats: 74 (46), 75 (47), 76 (48), 77 (49), 78 (51), 79 (52), 80 (50), 81 (53), 82 (54),
# 83 (55), 84 (57), 85 (58), 86 (59), 87 (61), 88 (63), 89 (64), 90 (62), 91 (66), 92 (67), 93 (70),
# 94 (56), 95 (65), 96 (69), 97 (73), 98 (71), 99 (72), 101 (60), 102 (68), 990970 (27), 990992
# (26), 991162 (28), 991172 (29).
#
# Each pair is hard for correct rounding: pow's exact result is a double or a midpoint between two
# doubles (the last two ranges, whose y is a multiple of 1/16, which HardCasePairsTest rechecks with
# BigInteger arithmetic of its own), or lies near one, by N identical bits after the round bit, N
# the source's `# N` annotation (the first three ranges). That annotation is the source's claim: the
# test checks those pairs' parse and count only, since rechecking N needs x**y to well over 100 bits
# after the round bit.
#
# e_pow.c does not round correctly (its error is below one ulp), so these pairs are no harder for a
# port that follows fdlibm's operations than any other pair; their use is that a dropped correction
# term or a reassociated sum, a change far below one ulp, is most likely to flip the result exactly
# at them. They are compared with StrictMath like every hard case, and nothing else is claimed of
# StrictMath's value.
#
# Written by the same run: 848 pairs.
# arity: 2
